forecaster_note: Long-period S swell is in, mixed with mid-period energy — a wait between the bigger sets and some power when they come. Light N breeze at dawn, cleanest at the N corners and S-facing spots; NE from mid-morning, so head to sheltered S-facing banks later. Find a good bank/reef or it can be a bit straight. — Surfline forecaster (Wed 30 Sep)

wind.summary: Light NNW 7 kph — offshore at dawn, cross-shore by 9am. Swings NE onshore ~14 kph from noon, 23 kph (gusts ~34) by 3pm.

shark.summary: No shark detections at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly — or anywhere Palm Beach to Manly — in the last 24h. Feed is current (newest statewide detection minutes old; 47 real detections statewide in 24h, none on the Northern Beaches).

days.label: Today
days.note: Solid long-period S groundswell in (3.7ft @ 16s, 595 kJ — real power) on a light N/NW dawn. Long Reef and Curl Curl are the picks — S-facing, they use it. Dee Why cops the dead-S 183° angle and wraps badly. Sets have a wait, so find a bank. Best ~7–11am (high tide 10:14am); NE onshore from noon, 23 kph by 3pm.

swells.label: Minor NE swell — the good angle

dee-why.window: Light NNW till ~9am, cross-shore after, NE onshore from noon. Dead-S 183° wraps badly here — the 16s period helps, but it'll be smaller and inconsistent vs the S exposures. Pick the peaks the small NE 69° helps.

tip.label: Dead S — skip the Point rights
tip.text: Dominant energy is dead-S (~183°), the angle that doesn't work at the Point. Frontside rights are a trap on it; use backside lefts when the S is doing the work and take peaks with some NE in them. Long 16s period gives the odd solid set — be patient.

swells.label: Minor NE swell — the good angle

long-reef.window: Best of the four: S-facing reef, uses the 3.7ft/16s S swell head-on. Light offshore till ~9am; stays cleaner than most into the arvo. Power in the sets with a wait between — mind the size on the bigger ones.

tip.label: Sit wide, pick your bomb
tip.text: 595 kJ at 16s is real power. Frontside rights off the reef — sit a touch wider than usual, let the first of the set go and take the one with shape. Paddle strong, commit early.

swells.label: Minor NE swell — the good angle

curl-curl.window: Big S-swell magnet: head to overhead with light N early. Best 7–10am before the NE lumps it up. Find a good bank or it can be a bit straight.

tip.label: Find the bank
tip.text: Solid and a bit straight if you sit on the wrong bank. Look for the peak that's holding shape and take the shoulder — the long period gives real push.

swells.label: Minor NE swell — the good angle

manly.window: Sheltered from the S so much smaller — camera-confirmed waist to chest. Cross-shore N breeze, tidiest when the NE comes in later.

tip.label: Sheltered fallback
tip.text: Least S energy of the four — softer, but the cleanest option if you can't stomach the size or the arvo NE arrives.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Easing S swell plus short-period NE wind wave — peaky, fun-sized: chest to maybe head at S exposures, smaller elsewhere. Cleanest early with light NW (8–10 kph), NE picks up late morning. Long Reef first, Curl Curl second. Sizes estimated from the forecaster text.

days.note: Fri looks like small peaky NE (waist–chest) with NW mornings. Sat/Sun hinge on a coastal low expected to form right on the coast — could turn on decent surf or a mess; the forecaster can't call it yet. Recheck Friday. Daylight saving starts Sun 4 Oct (clocks forward 2am) — dawn arrives an hour 'later'.
